# Tool reference

Every tool, grouped the way the servers load them. **Read** tools are the only ones a read-only server lists (`SMARTERMAIL_READ_ONLY`, on by default); **write** tools appear once it is turned off. **Destructive** writes delete, disable or disconnect something. MCP clients see the same marks as `readOnlyHint` / `destructiveHint`.

## Mailbox tools (59: 23 read, 36 write)

Served by **smartermail-mcp-user** and by the agent for mailbox and domain-admin accounts.

### Calendar

| Tool | Kind | Description |

| `delete_calendar_event` | write, destructive | Delete a calendar event |
| `get_calendar_event` | read | Get a calendar event for a given folder ID and event ID |
| `get_calendar_events` | read | Get calendar events for a given folder ID and date range |
| `new_or_update_calendar_event` | write | Create a new calendar event or update an existing one |
| `respond_to_meeting` | write | Respond to a meeting invitation (accept, decline, or tentative) |

### Mail

| Tool | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `create_draft` | write | Save an email as a draft without sending |
| `download_email_attachment` | read | Fetch an email attachment (filenames from get_email_attachments). Text attachments come back as text; binary ones as base64 when includeBase64=true (up to 5 MB). On a local server that shares your filesystem, savePath writes the file there instead. |
| `forward_email` | write | Forward an email message to other recipients |
| `get_email_attachments` | read | List an email's attachments: filename, contentType (from the file name), approximate size (SmarterMail rounds to KB) and the content IDs of images embedded inline in the body. Read a text attachment with read_email_part; download_email_attachment fetches any of them. |
| `get_email_message` | read | Get a specific email message by UID and folder |
| `get_emails` | read | Get email metadata like subject, from, date, id, read, flagged, etc. from a specific folder with optional search and pagination |
| `move_emails` | write | Move emails to a different folder |
| `read_email_part` | read | Inventory, window, or grep any part of an email. Omit part for an inventory of html/plain/text/headers/attachments with sizes. Set part (html, plain, text derived from HTML, headers, or attachment:<filename>) to read a window with offset/limit. Set pattern to grep (literal by default; isRegex=true for regex). Window responses include totalChars, nextOffset, and hasMore so you can page through large bodies. |
| `remove_emails` | write, destructive | Remove emails from the system |
| `reply_to_email` | write | Reply to an email message |
| `send_draft` | write | Send a previously saved draft email |
| `send_email` | write | Send a simple email |
| `send_email_with_attachments` | write | Send an email with previously uploaded attachments. Use upload_attachment first, then pass its attachmentGuid here. Inline images uploaded with inline=true are shown where the body has <img src="cid:..."> with their htmlReference. |
| `set_email_properties` | write | Mark emails as read/unread, flagged/unflagged, or add tags |
| `upload_attachment` | write | Upload a file to attach to an email, then send it with send_email_with_attachments using the returned attachmentGuid. Give the file as exactly one of: base64Content (any file, base64-encoded), text (a text file's contents, e.g. .txt/.csv/.ics/.html) or filePath (only on a local server that shares your filesystem). For an image shown inside the HTML body, set inline=true and use the returned htmlReference as the src: <img src="cid:...">. SmarterMail assigns the content ID, so always use the returned value. Several files go in one email by passing the first call's attachmentGuid to the next calls. |

### Settings

| Tool | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `block_senders` | write | Block email senders to prevent delivery. Accepts email addresses or domains. |
| `check_sender_blocked` | read | Check if a sender email address is blocked |
| `check_sender_trusted` | read | Check if a sender email address is trusted (whitelisted) |
| `create_content_filter` | write | Create a content filter (inbox rule).  Conditions JSON format: [{"fieldType": 0, "filterType": 2, "searchArguments": ["value"]}] - fieldType: 0=FromAddress, 1=FromDomain, 3=WordsInSubject, 4=WordsInBody, 10=ToAddress, 16=HasAttachments, 17=AttachmentFilename - filterType: 0=Equals, 1=DoesntEqual, 2=Contains, 3=DoesntContain  Actions JSON format: [{"actionType": 4, "argument": "FolderName"}] - actionType: 1=Delete, 4=MoveToFolder (arg=folder), 5=AddHeader (arg=Header:Value), 6=PrefixSubject (arg=prefix), 7=Forward (arg=email), 8=MarkAsRead  Example: Create filter to move newsletters to a folder:   title: "Newsletter Filter"   matchType: "And"   conditions: [{"fieldType": 0, "filterType": 2, "searchArguments": ["newsletter@"]}]   actions: [{"actionType": 4, "argument": "Newsletters"}] |
| `create_content_filter_simple` | write | Create a content filter (inbox rule) using simple human-readable descriptions instead of JSON.  Condition examples (separate multiple with semicolons):   'from contains newsletter@' - match sender address containing text   'from equals user@example.com' - match exact sender address   'from domain is example.com' - match sender domain   'subject contains invoice' - match subject line   'body contains unsubscribe' - match email body   'to contains sales@' - match recipient   'has attachments' - match emails with attachments   'attachment name contains .pdf' - match attachment filename   'attachment extension is pdf' - match attachment extension  Action examples (separate multiple with semicolons):   'move to Newsletters' - move to folder   'delete' - delete the email   'mark as read' - mark as read   'forward to bob@example.com' - forward to address   'prefix subject with [NEWS]' - add prefix to subject   'set priority high' - set priority (high/normal/low)   'flag' - flag for follow up  Supports negation: 'from does not contain X', 'subject doesn't contain X' |
| `delete_content_filters` | write, destructive | Delete content filters by ID |
| `get_content_filters` | read | Get all content filters (inbox rules). Returns filter groups with their conditions and actions.  Condition Field Types: 0=FromAddress, 1=FromDomain, 3=WordsInSubject, 4=WordsInBody, 7=WordsInTo, 10=ToAddress, 16=HasAttachments, 17=AttachmentFilename Comparison Types: 0=Equals, 1=DoesntEqual, 2=Contains, 3=DoesntContain Action Types: 1=Delete, 4=MoveToFolder, 5=AddHeader, 6=PrefixSubject, 7=Forward, 8=MarkAsRead Match Types: 0=And (all conditions), 1=Or (any condition) |
| `run_content_filters` | write | Run content filters against a folder to process existing emails |
| `set_trusted_senders` | write, destructive | Set trusted senders (whitelist) to bypass spam filtering. Accepts email addresses and/or domains. |
| `unblock_senders` | write | Unblock previously blocked senders. Accepts email addresses or domains. |
| `update_content_filter` | write | Update an existing content filter. Only provided fields will be updated.  See create_content_filter for conditions and actions JSON format. |

## Domain-admin tools (107: 44 read, 63 write)

Served by **smartermail-mcp-user** when the account is a domain admin (`SMARTERMAIL_DOMAIN_TOOLS`, default `auto`), and by the agent for domain-admin accounts. They act on the signed-in admin's own domain.

### Domain Admin

| Tool | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `domain_create_alias` | write | Create an email alias in your domain that delivers mail to one or more target addresses. |
| `domain_create_user` | write | Create a new user in your domain. Domain default settings apply to anything not given here. |
| `domain_delete_alias` | write, destructive | Permanently delete an alias from your domain. Mail sent to it will no longer be delivered. |
| `domain_delete_users` | write, destructive | Permanently delete one or more users in your domain and all of their mail data. Cannot delete the primary domain admin or yourself. This cannot be undone. |
| `domain_disable_users` | write, destructive | Disable (or re-enable) one or more users in your domain. A disabled user cannot sign in. |
| `domain_get_alias` | read | Get the full configuration of one alias in your domain: targets, display name, GAL visibility, internal-only, sending permission and more. |
| `domain_get_info` | read | Get basic information about your domain: name, hostname, enabled state, user/alias/list counts and limits, and disk usage. |
| `domain_get_settings` | read | Get the full configuration of your domain (general settings, security options, catch-all, auto-clean, feature permissions). Large response. Password and secret values are redacted. |
| `domain_get_user` | read | Get the full account details of one user in your domain: settings, permissions, security flags, mailbox size and last login. |
| `domain_list_aliases` | read | List the email aliases in your domain with their target addresses. |
| `domain_list_users` | read | List the users in your domain with username, email address, full name, disabled state, domain-admin flag, mailbox size and last login. |
| `domain_update_alias` | write | Update an existing alias in your domain. Only the fields you pass are changed. Passing targets replaces the whole target list. |
| `domain_update_user` | write | Update an existing user in your domain. Only the fields you pass are changed; everything else is kept. |

### Domain Mailing List

| Tool | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `domain_add_mailing_list_posters` | write | Add email addresses to a mailing list's approved posters (allowed to post) or to its banned users (may neither post nor subscribe). Requires a domain admin account. |
| `domain_add_mailing_list_subscribers` | write | Subscribe one or more email addresses to a mailing list, as regular subscribers or as digest subscribers. If the list uses double opt-in, SmarterMail may email each address a confirmation first. Requires a domain admin account. |
| `domain_clear_subscriber_bounces` | write | Reset a subscriber's bounce count to zero, e.g. after their mailbox problem was fixed, so the list stops treating them as bouncing. Requires a domain admin account. |
| `domain_create_mailing_list` | write | Create a new mailing list in your domain. Anything not given here uses SmarterMail's defaults; change more with domain_update_mailing_list. Requires a domain admin account. |
| `domain_delete_mailing_lists` | write, destructive | Permanently delete one or more mailing lists, with all their subscribers, posters and settings. This cannot be undone. Requires a domain admin account. |
| `domain_delete_subscriber_fields` | write, destructive | Delete one or more custom subscriber fields, and every subscriber's value for them. This cannot be undone. Requires a domain admin account. |
| `domain_get_mailing_list` | read | Get the full settings of one mailing list (posting permissions, digest, double opt-in, subject prefix, throttling, custom To/From/Reply-To, unsubscribe text, spam filtering, GAL visibility…) together with its counts of subscribers, digest subscribers, posters, banned users, custom fields and system messages. The posting password, if any, is redacted. Requires a domain admin account. |
| `domain_get_mailing_list_messages` | read | Get a mailing list's system message templates (welcome, goodbye, opt-in confirmation, error replies…): name, subject, body and last-modified date. Use the name with domain_update_mailing_list_message. Requires a domain admin account. |
| `domain_get_mailing_list_subscriber` | read | Get one subscriber's details across your domain's mailing lists: which lists and digests they are subscribed to, custom field values, bounce address, bounce count and history, and the log of list messages sent to them. Requires a domain admin account. |
| `domain_list_mailing_list_posters` | read | Search a mailing list's approved posters (addresses allowed to post) or its banned users (addresses that may neither post nor subscribe), with paging. Requires a domain admin account. |
| `domain_list_mailing_lists` | read | List the mailing lists in your domain: id, list address, description, moderator, status, posting permissions, digest/double opt-in flags and subscriber, digest, poster and banned-user counts. Use the id with the other mailing list tools. Requires a domain admin account. |
| `domain_list_subscriber_fields` | read | List the custom subscriber fields defined for your domain's mailing lists: id, name and default value. Requires a domain admin account. |
| `domain_remove_mailing_list_posters` | write, destructive | Remove email addresses from a mailing list's approved posters or from its banned users. Requires a domain admin account. |
| `domain_remove_mailing_list_subscribers` | write, destructive | Unsubscribe one or more email addresses from a mailing list (regular or digest subscribers). Requires a domain admin account. |
| `domain_save_subscriber_field` | write | Create a custom subscriber field for your domain's mailing lists, or rename one / change its default value. Requires a domain admin account. |
| `domain_search_mailing_list_subscribers` | read | Search the subscribers of a mailing list, with paging. Returns the total match count and the page of subscribers (address, bounce count, last edit). Requires a domain admin account. |
| `domain_send_mailing_list_digest` | write | Send a mailing list's pending digest right now, emailing every digest subscriber, instead of waiting for its schedule. Requires a domain admin account. |
| `domain_update_mailing_list` | write | Change a mailing list's settings. Only the fields you pass are changed; everything else is kept. For settings without their own parameter, pass them in settingsJson using the field names domain_get_mailing_list returns. Requires a domain admin account. |
| `domain_update_mailing_list_message` | write | Change one of a mailing list's system message templates (see domain_get_mailing_list_messages for the names). Some messages have no subject; leave subject out for those. Requires a domain admin account. |
| `domain_update_mailing_list_subscriber` | write | Change one subscriber: set custom field values, and/or replace which of your domain's lists and digests they are subscribed to. Only what you pass is changed. Requires a domain admin account. |

| Tool | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `domain_add_domain_alias` | write | Add a domain alias: mail to <anything>@aliasName will be delivered to the matching mailbox in your domain. Optionally require the alias's MX records to point here first. |
| `domain_check_address_available` | read | Check whether an address (local part, e.g. 'sales') is free to use for a new user or alias in your domain. success:true means it is available. |
| `domain_create_shared_resource` | write | Create a domain-level shared resource: a shared calendar, conference room, piece of equipment, address book, task list or note list. Rooms and equipment can be booked by inviting their email alias. |
| `domain_create_signature` | write | Create a domain signature template. The text may be HTML and may contain SmarterMail signature variables. Assign it with domain_set_signature_mapping. |
| `domain_delete_domain_aliases` | write, destructive | Delete one or more domain aliases. Mail to those domain names will no longer be delivered to this domain. |
| `domain_delete_event_hooks` | write, destructive | Delete one or more event hooks. They stop firing immediately. |
| `domain_delete_shared_resource` | write, destructive | Permanently delete a domain shared resource and everything in it (events, contacts, tasks or notes). Cannot be undone. |
| `domain_delete_signature` | write, destructive | Permanently delete a domain signature template. Anyone mapped to it stops getting it on outgoing mail. |
| `domain_get_event_catalog` | read | Get the event types an event hook can fire on (with their conditions, arguments and available actions) and, optionally, the variables usable in action text. Read this before creating an event hook. Large response. |
| `domain_get_forward_blacklist` | read | Get the forwarding blacklist: addresses and domains that users in your domain may not auto-forward mail to. |
| `domain_get_permissions` | read | Get the feature permissions the system administrator has granted your domain (which settings and features the domain may use or override). |
| `domain_get_signature_mappings` | read | Get which signature template applies to which user, alias, domain alias or the whole domain. type: 1 DomainAlias, 2 Domain, 3 Alias, 4 User, 5 SmtpAccount. mapOption: 0 None, 1 UsePrimary, 2 SignatureSpecified (signatureGuid), 3 UseDomainDefault. |
| `domain_list_domain_aliases` | read | List the domain aliases of your domain: other domain names (e.g. example.net) whose mail is delivered to this domain's mailboxes. |
| `domain_list_event_hooks` | read | List event hooks (automated actions such as notifications that fire on mail events). By default lists the domain-level hooks; pass an owner to list one user's hooks. |
| `domain_list_shared_resources` | read | List the domain-level shared resources: shared calendars, conference rooms, equipment, address books, task and note lists, with their folderId, type, email alias, enabled state, booking window and who has access. |
| `domain_list_signatures` | read | List the domain's email signature templates (id, guid, name, HTML text, isDefault) and whether a domain signature is in use. |
| `domain_rename_domain_alias` | write | Rename a domain alias (e.g. example.net → example.org). Optionally require the new name's MX records to point here first. |
| `domain_save_event_hook` | write | Create an event hook, or replace an existing one, from a full event-hook JSON object (name, enabled, eventID/eventGroup, conditions[], actions[] with inputs[]; the shape domain_list_event_hooks returns). Get valid events, conditions and actions from domain_get_event_catalog. To edit a hook, read it, change it, and pass it back with its id and isNew:false. |
| `domain_set_catch_all` | write | Set the catch-all: the alias that receives mail sent to any address in your domain that does not exist. Pass an empty value to turn the catch-all off. |
| `domain_set_event_hook_enabled` | write | Turn an existing event hook on or off without changing anything else about it. |
| `domain_set_signature_mapping` | write | Assign a signature to a user, alias, domain alias or the whole domain, or remove such an assignment. Other mappings are kept. |
| `domain_update_settings` | write | Change domain settings. Pass a JSON object of only the settings to change, using the property names domain_get_settings returns (e.g. {"enableMailForwarding":false} or {"externalSenderOverrideSettings":{"enabled":true}}). Nested objects are merged, arrays and plain values replace. Everything you do not mention is kept. Unknown names are refused. |
| `domain_update_shared_resource` | write | Rename a domain shared resource and/or change who can access it. For access, the users you list get the given level; pass removeUsers to take access away. Group access and anyone not mentioned are kept. |
| `domain_update_signature` | write | Change a domain signature template's name, text or default flag. Only the fields you pass change. |
| `domain_verify_domain_alias_mx` | read | Check that a domain alias's MX records point at this mail server. Only checks DNS; changes nothing. Use after adding a domain alias. |

### Domain Security

| Tool | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `domain_add_content_filter` | write | Add a content filter that applies to every user in your domain. conditions: JSON array of {fieldType, filterType, searchArguments, applyLogicalNot?, isWildcard?}; fieldType is a name such as FromAddress, FromDomain, WordsInSubject, WordsInBody, WordsInSubjectOrBody, WordsInFrom, WordsInTo, WordsInHeaders, ToAddress, ToDomain, CcAddress, AttHas, AttFilename, AttExtension, MessageSizeOver, MessageSizeUnder, SendingServerIP, SpamWeight, IsAuthenticated, AutomatedMessage; filterType is Equals, DoesntEqual, Contains or DoesntContain; searchArguments is a list of strings. actions: JSON array of {actionType, argument?}; actionType is one of NoAction, Delete, Bounce, MoveToFolder (argument = folder name), AddHeader (argument = header line), PrefixSubject (argument = prefix text), Forward (argument = address), Read, SetPriority, FollowUp. Example: conditions=[{"fieldType":"FromDomain","filterType":"Equals","searchArguments":["spammy.example"]}], actions=[{"actionType":"Delete"}]. |
| `domain_create_dkim_rollover` | write | Start a DKIM key rotation: generates a new key pair that stays pending (the current key keeps signing) until its DNS record is published and verified with domain_verify_dkim(rollover=true). Returns the new selector and public key to publish. |
| `domain_delete_content_filters` | write, destructive | Permanently delete domain-level content filters by id. They stop applying to every user in your domain. |
| `domain_delete_dkim_rollover` | write, destructive | Cancel a pending DKIM key rotation: deletes the pending rollover key without activating it. The active key is unaffected. |
| `domain_disable_dkim` | write, destructive | Turn off DKIM signing for your domain. Any pending DKIM key is deleted. Outgoing mail stops being signed immediately, which can hurt deliverability where receivers expect DKIM. |
| `domain_enable_dkim` | write | Turn on DKIM signing for your domain. If no DKIM key exists yet, a pending key is created; publish its selector and public key in DNS (see domain_get_dkim), then run domain_verify_dkim. Without forceActivation an active key that fails DNS validation is moved back to pending. |
| `domain_get_dkim` | read | Get your domain's DKIM signing configuration: whether signing is active, the selector and public key to publish in DNS, key size, canonicalization, signed header fields, and any pending rollover key with its DNS status. Private keys are never returned. |
| `domain_get_security_settings` | read | Get your domain's sender and login security: the domain whitelist (addresses and domains that bypass spam filtering), the forwarding blocklist, login country restrictions, the IP access list, SMTP authentication / SSL / HSTS / TLS / SRS requirements, sending throttles and the external-sender warning settings. |
| `domain_get_spam_settings` | read | Get your domain's spam filtering: whether the domain overrides the server defaults, the low/medium/high spam weight thresholds and the action taken at each level, the server defaults, and the relay/forward spam options. |
| `domain_get_user_login_ips` | read | List the IP addresses a user in your domain has signed in from, with location and last-login time, grouped by protocol/category. Useful when investigating a compromised account. |
| `domain_list_content_filters` | read | List the domain-level content filters, which apply to every user in your domain: id, title, order, enabled state, match type, conditions and actions (enum values are numeric; see domain_add_content_filter for the names). |
| `domain_list_spam_checks` | read | List the DNS blocklists (RBL / URIBL) used for spam checking: name, lookup domain, whether each is enabled for incoming and outgoing SMTP, and how results are weighted. |
| `domain_move_content_filter` | write | Move a domain-level content filter one place up (evaluated earlier) or down in the processing order. |
| `domain_test_dkim_dns` | read | Check whether a DKIM public key is correctly published in DNS. Only performs a DNS lookup; changes nothing. By default tests the active key; set which='pending' to test the rollover key, or pass selector and publicKey to test any key. |
| `domain_update_content_filter` | write | Change a domain-level content filter. Only what you pass changes; conditions and actions, when given, replace the filter's whole list (same format as domain_add_content_filter). Use domain_list_content_filters to find the id. |
| `domain_update_dkim_settings` | write | Change how your domain signs mail with DKIM (does not change the key). Only the options you pass change; the rest keep their current values. |
| `domain_update_spam_settings` | write | Change your domain's spam thresholds and actions. Only the values you pass change. Changing weights or actions turns on the domain override of the server defaults unless overrideActive=false is passed. The server administrator may not allow domains to override spam actions. Actions: NoAction, Delete, Bounce, MoveToFolder (argument = folder name), AddHeader (argument = header line), PrefixSubject (argument = prefix text), Forward (argument = address), Read, SetPriority, FollowUp. |
| `domain_update_whitelist` | write, destructive | Change the domain whitelist: senders (email addresses) and sending domains that bypass spam filtering for every user in your domain. mode 'add' (default) and 'remove' edit the current list; 'replace' sets it to exactly what you pass. Whitelisting a sender lets its spam through, so add only senders you trust. |
| `domain_verify_dkim` | write | Have SmarterMail validate a DKIM key against DNS and update its status. rollover=false checks the active key; rollover=true checks the pending rollover key and, if DNS matches, makes it the active signing key. Can change which key signs mail. For a lookup that changes nothing, use domain_test_dkim_dns. |

### Domain User

| Tool | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `domain_create_user_group` | write | Create a user group in your domain. Groups are used to assign permissions, signatures and shared resources to several users at once. |
| `domain_delete_user_groups` | write, destructive | Delete one or more user groups in your domain. The member users are not deleted, but lose whatever the group granted them. |
| `domain_disable_two_factor` | write, destructive | Turn off two-step authentication for one user in your domain, e.g. when they lost their authenticator device. They can sign in with just their password until they set it up again. |
| `domain_disconnect_users` | write, destructive | Force users in your domain to sign in again: ends their webmail sessions and/or drops their open protocol connections (IMAP, POP, ActiveSync, …). Useful after a password change or a suspected compromise. |
| `domain_expire_user_passwords` | write, destructive | Mark the passwords of one or more users in your domain as expired, so they must choose a new one at their next sign-in. |
| `domain_get_account_counts` | read | Get a quick overview of your domain's size: number of users, aliases, administrators, groups, ActiveSync and MAPI/EWS mailboxes and mailing lists, with the domain's limits. |
| `domain_get_last_login_times` | read | Get the last login time of every user in your domain, with enabled and domain-admin flags. Useful for finding inactive accounts. |
| `domain_get_mailbox_forwarding` | read | Get where one user's incoming mail is forwarded: the forward-to addresses, whether a copy is kept, whether original recipients are kept, and how spam is handled. |
| `domain_get_password_policy` | read | Get your domain's password policy: the server defaults and the domain's overrides (minimum length, required character classes, common-password and username checks, password history, expiration and grace period). |
| `domain_get_user_connections` | read | Get who is connected in your domain: per-user connection counts, last login (overall and webmail), last authenticating IP and protocol, plus domain-wide counts per protocol (webmail, IMAP, POP, SMTP, ActiveSync, MAPI/EWS, XMPP, WebDAV). |
| `domain_get_user_defaults` | read | Get the default settings applied to NEW users created in your domain (mailbox size, protocol access, feature permissions, GAL visibility, password lock, auto-clean and more). |
| `domain_get_user_group` | read | Get one user group in your domain by id: name, enabled state and member usernames. |
| `domain_get_user_indexing_status` | read | Get the search-index status of one user's mailbox: whether it is indexing, items indexed and still to index, last indexed time and current status. |
| `domain_get_user_mail_settings` | read | Get one user's mail settings: can receive mail, forwarding enabled, ActiveSync / MAPI-EWS enabled, mailbox size limit, sending throttles, auto-clean rules, blocked and trusted senders, spam and calendar options. |
| `domain_get_user_statuses` | read | Get the account health of users in your domain: enabled, two-factor enabled, expired password, password-policy violations, indexing / migrating state, authentication type and critical errors. Paginated. |
| `domain_list_password_issues` | read | List users in your domain with password problems: 'noncompliant' (password breaks the current policy; shows which rules), 'expired' (must change before signing in) or 'aged' (approaching or past the maximum age). Paginated. |
| `domain_list_protocol_mailboxes` | read | List the mailboxes in your domain that have ActiveSync or MAPI/EWS (Outlook) access enabled, with display name and last sync time. These are licensed per mailbox. |
| `domain_list_user_groups` | read | List the user groups in your domain (id, name, enabled, member usernames). Pass a username to list only the groups that user belongs to. |
| `domain_recalculate_mailbox_sizes` | write | Recount the disk usage of one or more mailboxes in your domain, for when the reported size is out of sync with what is actually stored. |
| `domain_reindex_users` | write | Rebuild the search index of one or more mailboxes in your domain. Use when search results are missing or wrong. Runs in the background and can take a while for large mailboxes. |
| `domain_rename_user` | write | Change a user's username (and so their email address) in your domain. Mail, settings and folders are kept. The old address stops working unless you add an alias for it. You cannot rename yourself with this tool. |
| `domain_resync_user_devices` | write | Force the connected devices (ActiveSync and other sync clients) of one or more users in your domain to resynchronise. Use to fix devices that stopped syncing. |
| `domain_search_accounts` | read | Search the users and aliases of your domain together, with status (enabled / disabled / errored), account type, authentication type and ActiveSync / MAPI-EWS flags. Paginated. |
| `domain_set_mailbox_forwarding` | write | Set where one user's incoming mail is forwarded. Only what you pass is changed. Pass an empty forwardTo list to stop forwarding. The user's mail settings must also allow forwarding (enableMailForwarding, see domain_update_user_mail_settings). |
| `domain_set_protocol_access` | write | Turn protocols on or off for one or more users in your domain. Only the protocols you pass are changed. ActiveSync and MAPI/EWS are licensed per mailbox and count against the domain's limits. |
| `domain_set_user_group_membership` | write | Add one user to, and/or remove them from, user groups in your domain. |
| `domain_update_password_policy` | write | Change your domain's password policy. Only the rules you pass are changed; everything else is kept. Stricter rules affect existing users at their next password change and show up in domain_list_password_issues. |
| `domain_update_user_defaults` | write | Change the default settings for NEW users in your domain (see domain_get_user_defaults for the field names), e.g. {"hideFromGal":true}. Only the fields you pass are changed. Existing users are not affected. |
| `domain_update_user_group` | write | Rename, enable/disable, or replace the member list of a user group in your domain. Only what you pass is changed. |
| `domain_update_user_mail_settings` | write | Change one user's mail settings (see domain_get_user_mail_settings for the field names), e.g. {"canReceiveMail":false}, {"maxSize":0}, {"throttleSettings":{"messagesPerHour":500}} or {"blockedSenders":["spam@example.com"]}. The fields you pass are merged into the current settings; lists you pass replace the current list. |

### Log Search

| Tool | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `search_log_files` | read | Search server log files by type, date range, and search term. A busy day of a log can be megabytes, so the result is a WINDOW (maxChars, default 20000): narrow first with a one-day range and a specific search term (the server filters on it), optionally 'contains' to keep only matching lines, then page. The window shows the most recent part first (tail=true); the result reports totalChars, returnedChars, hasMore and nextOffset - call again with offset=nextOffset to read further back (tail=true) or forward (tail=false). Available log types: smtpLog, delivery, imapLog, popLog, spamChecks, contentfilter, administrative, generalErrors, event, ews, ewsRetrieval, activeSync, calendars, certificates, autodiscover, imapRetrieval, popRetrieval, indexing, ldapLog, activation, mailinglists, maintenance, mapi, messageId, oab, routingRules, conversion, autoCleanFolders, webdav, xmppLog |
